Why go: Ang Thong at sailing pace

Most Ang Thong trips are about speed: a fast boat, a tight timetable and a crowded beach. The Naga day is the opposite. You travel on a 30 m wooden gulet with a sun deck of 20 loungers, eat breakfast and lunch at a proper table, and come back with the sun going down behind the islands.

Time in the park covers the two big sights: the Koh Wua Talab viewpoint, a steep climb with ropes over the whole archipelago, and the Emerald Lake on Koh Mae Ko, a saltwater lagoon inside the island.

Life on board

Naga was built in 2005 as a two-masted Turkish-style gulet and has six air-conditioned cabins, a saloon with a dining area, a covered aft lounge and a full galley. Breakfast is served after departure and a Thai buffet lunch on board between the two island stops, with fruit, snacks and soft drinks all day. Towels and snorkel gear are provided; kayaks can be hired on the beach at Koh Wua Talab. Bring grippy shoes for the viewpoint climb.

Who it suits

  • Couples and families who want Ang Thong without a speedboat.
  • Guests who like comfort: shade, towels and meals on board.
  • Photographers who want the sunset sail back.

Who should choose something else

  • Guests short on time: our Ang Thong speedboat tour is quicker and cheaper.
  • Anyone wanting fewer guests and more speed: the Ang Thong VIP tour.
  • Overnight lovers: our Ang Thong overnight stays in the park.

Good to know

  • Season: Ang Thong closes every year from 1 November to 15 December; book from 16 December.
  • Long day: pickup at 06:50 and back after sunset.
  • Booking: online booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thai time; confirmation by email or WhatsApp.
